why_caution: Very much a nightlife-and-expat zone
local_tip: Juffair has the widest choice of late-night dining and bars in the city

name: Mutrah
why_fits: The old harbor district of the Corniche, the labyrinthine souq and the fish market
why_caution: Spread far from the modern city center
local_tip: Walk the Mutrah Corniche at dusk, then dive into the lantern-lit souq

name: Qurum
why_fits: A central district with the city's main beach, a big park and shopping malls
why_caution: A car-reliant, spread-out area
local_tip: Qurum Beach and its adjacent park are the easiest family spot in the city

name: Al Khuwair
why_fits: A convenient central district of hotels, ministries, malls and the Grand Mosque nearby
why_caution: A functional modern strip along the highway
local_tip: The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque nearby is open to respectful visitors each morning

name: Al-Balad
why_fits: The bustling downtown of the Roman theatre, souks and old cafes, the city's authentic core
why_caution: Steep, busy streets and quiet after dark
local_tip: Climb to the Citadel above downtown for Roman ruins and a sweeping city view

name: Jabal Amman
why_fits: The hip hillside around Rainbow Street, full of cafes, galleries and the Friday market
why_caution: Congested and lively along Rainbow Street on weekends
local_tip: The Souk Jara Friday market on Rainbow Street is a great local browse

name: Abdoun
why_fits: An upscale, leafy embassy district of smart cafes and restaurants west of downtown
why_caution: Removed from the historic sights, reliant on taxis
local_tip: It's the calmest, most polished base, an easy drive from the downtown ruins

name: Jaffa
why_fits: The ancient port of stone lanes, the flea market and sea views, fused onto the modern city
why_caution: Busy flea-market crowds and cobbled lanes
local_tip: Get lost in the Jaffa flea market's antique stalls, then watch sunset from the old port

name: Florentin
why_fits: The gritty-cool southern district of street art, cheap bars and a young, creative crowd
why_caution: Rough-edged and noisy at night
local_tip: Florentin is the city's best area for street art and a low-cost night out

name: Neve Tzedek
best_for: Couples seeking a calmer base|Culture lovers
why_fits: The city's first neighborhood, now a charming quarter of boutiques, galleries and low lanes
why_caution: Small and pricey, with few big sights
local_tip: Walk pedestrian Shabazi Street, the heart of this pretty low-rise quarter

name: Old Medina
why_fits: The walled old town beside the port, a maze of markets right by the Hassan II Mosque
why_caution: Rougher and less polished than the new city
local_tip: Walk from the old medina to the vast Hassan II Mosque on its ocean platform

name: Maarif
why_fits: A modern central district of shopping, restaurants and the Morocco Mall nearby
why_caution: A busy commercial area rather than a scenic one
local_tip: Maarif's cafe terraces are the classic Casablanca spot for people-watching

name: Ain Diab
why_fits: The Corniche seafront strip of beach clubs, restaurants and the city's nightlife
why_caution: A car ride from the center, pricier beachfront
local_tip: The Corniche beach clubs are where Casablanca comes to relax by the Atlantic

name: Medina
why_fits: The UNESCO old town, a dense maze of souks, mosques and the Zitouna, the city's soul
why_caution: A tight labyrinth, easy to get lost in
local_tip: Follow the covered souks from the main gate up toward the Zitouna Mosque

name: Ville Nouvelle
why_fits: The French-built new town along Avenue Habib Bourguiba, with cafes, hotels and the theatre
why_caution: A busy central avenue
local_tip: The tree-lined Avenue Bourguiba is the city's main promenade and cafe strip

name: Sidi Bou Said
why_fits: The famous blue-and-white clifftop village overlooking the Mediterranean, north of the city
why_caution: A 20km trip from central Tunis
local_tip: Come to Sidi Bou Said for sunset over the sea from a blue-shuttered cafe terrace

name: Downtown
why_fits: The faded-grand center around Raml Station, old cafes and the great new Library of Alexandria
why_caution: Congested and worn at the edges
local_tip: Visit the striking modern Bibliotheca Alexandrina on the waterfront

name: Corniche
why_fits: The long Mediterranean seafront of the Corniche, from the Citadel to the city beaches
why_caution: A city seafront rather than a resort beach
local_tip: Walk the Corniche to the Qaitbay Citadel, built on the old lighthouse site

name: Smouha
why_fits: A planned, greener residential district of wider streets and malls, calmer than downtown
why_caution: Away from the historic seafront
local_tip: It's a comfortable, quieter base with an easy tram or taxi to the Corniche

name: Osu
why_fits: The lively district around Oxford Street, packed with restaurants, bars and shops
why_caution: Congested and noisy along the main strip
local_tip: Osu's Oxford Street is the city's densest run of dining and nightlife

name: Airport Residential
why_fits: An upscale, leafy district of embassies, smart hotels and malls near the airport
why_caution: A quiet, affluent zone away from the street life
local_tip: It's the most comfortable base, minutes from the airport and good restaurants

name: Jamestown
why_fits: The historic colonial fishing quarter of the old lighthouse, forts and vibrant street murals
why_caution: A poorer, rougher area best explored with a local guide
local_tip: Climb the Jamestown lighthouse for a view over the old harbor and fishing boats

name: Piazza
why_fits: The old Italian-era quarter of Art Deco buildings, jewellers and historic cafes
why_caution: Congested and worn, high-altitude and hilly
local_tip: Sip a macchiato in a Piazza cafe, a lasting legacy of the Italian era

name: Bole
why_fits: The modern main artery near the airport, lined with hotels, malls and restaurants
why_caution: A busy road-oriented district
local_tip: Bole's location makes it the easiest, most comfortable first-visit base

name: Kazanchis
best_for: Business travelers|Couples seeking a calmer base
why_fits: A central district of hotels, UN offices and the national museum nearby
why_caution: A functional mixed district
local_tip: The National Museum here holds 'Lucy', the famous early-hominid skeleton

name: CBD
why_fits: The central business district of offices, markets and the nearby national museum
why_caution: Crowded by day and best avoided on foot after dark
local_tip: Base here for easy access, but arrange transport rather than walking at night

name: Westlands
why_fits: The lively upmarket district of malls, restaurants and the city's best nightlife
why_caution: Congested traffic and pricier than the center
local_tip: Westlands has the widest choice of international dining and bars in the city

name: Karen
why_fits: A leafy, upscale suburb of gardens and the Giraffe Centre and elephant orphanage nearby
why_caution: Well out of the center, reliant on driving
local_tip: The Giraffe Centre and Sheldrick elephant orphanage are both close by here

name: Nyarugenge
why_fits: The compact, remarkably clean city center of banks, hotels and the main market
why_caution: A hilly working center
local_tip: Kigali is famously clean and safe -- the walkable center reflects it

name: Kimihurura
why_fits: A hilltop district of embassies, smart restaurants and rooftop bars with city views
why_caution: Spread across hills, reliant on moto-taxis
local_tip: Watch the sunset over the hills from a Kimihurura rooftop bar

name: Nyamirambo
why_fits: The city's most vibrant, multicultural and affordable district, great for a walking tour
why_caution: Livelier and less polished than central Kigali
local_tip: Take the women-led Nyamirambo walking tour for a genuine local welcome

name: Victoria Island
why_fits: The commercial heart of banks, hotels, beaches and the best restaurants, on the lagoon
why_caution: Notorious traffic ('go-slow') and pricey
local_tip: Bar Beach and the Landmark beach area give VI a rare in-city stretch of sand

name: Ikoyi
why_fits: The most exclusive, leafy residential district of mansions, embassies and fine dining
why_caution: Very expensive and quiet
local_tip: It's the calmest, greenest and safest-feeling base in the city

name: Lekki
why_fits: A newer, planned peninsula of gated estates, malls, beaches and the conservation centre
why_caution: A long drive from the old city, traffic-heavy
local_tip: The Lekki Conservation Centre's long canopy walkway is a fine half-day out

name: Town Centre
why_fits: The colonial-era town of curio markets and the museum, the practical base for Victoria Falls
why_caution: A small, dusty town away from the falls themselves
local_tip: The town museum is a good primer before heading to the falls a few km away

name: Mosi-oa-Tunya Road
why_fits: The main road strip of backpacker lodges, hostels and tour operators toward the falls
why_caution: A functional strip rather than a scenic one
local_tip: This is where to book white-water rafting, bungee and safari day trips

name: Zambezi Riverfront
why_fits: The upstream riverfront of luxury lodges overlooking the Zambezi above the falls
why_caution: Remote and expensive, away from town
local_tip: Take a sunset river cruise from a riverfront lodge to spot hippos and elephants

name: Stone Town
why_fits: The UNESCO old town of carved doors, winding lanes, Swahili-Arab palaces and the night market
why_caution: A maze that's easy to get lost in; touristy
local_tip: Graze the Forodhani Gardens night market's grilled seafood by the water

name: Shangani
why_fits: The historic seafront corner of Stone Town, home to its grandest heritage hotels
why_caution: Right in the busy old town, pricier
local_tip: Its seafront hotels have the best sunset terraces over the Indian Ocean

name: Michenzani
why_fits: A local, authentic residential district just inland, well away from the tourist core
why_caution: Plain and short on sights or dining
local_tip: It offers a cheaper, genuinely local base a short walk from Stone Town

name: Blue Area
why_fits: The central commercial spine of offices, banks and restaurants running through the city
why_caution: A functional business strip
local_tip: It's the most central base, an easy drive to the Margalla Hills trails

name: F-7
why_fits: A leafy, upscale sector of markets (Jinnah Super), embassies and calm tree-lined streets
why_caution: A spread-out, car-reliant grid
local_tip: Hike Trail 5 into the Margalla Hills from the edge of the sector for city views

name: Saidpur Village
why_fits: A restored Mughal-era village on the Margalla hillside, now a cultural-and-dining spot
why_caution: Small, and mainly a day-visit destination
local_tip: Come up to Saidpur for dinner with the city lights spread out below

name: Vieux-Montreal
why_fits: The cobbled old town of Notre-Dame Basilica, the old port and heritage stone buildings
why_caution: Touristy and busy along the waterfront in summer
local_tip: See the Notre-Dame Basilica's blue-lit interior, then walk the Old Port

name: Plateau Mont-Royal
why_fits: The colorful, creative district of murals, terraces, bagel shops and buzzing Saint-Denis
why_caution: Lively and noisy on the main strips
local_tip: Grab a wood-fired Montreal bagel here, then picnic on Mount Royal nearby

name: Downtown
why_fits: The high-rise core of shopping, museums and the vast Underground City network
why_caution: A corporate center, quieter on weekends
local_tip: Duck into the Underground City to shop and move between blocks in bad weather

name: Vieux-Quebec
why_fits: The walled UNESCO old town of Chateau Frontenac, cobbled lanes and ramparts, storybook-pretty
why_caution: Steep, cobbled and very touristy in summer
local_tip: Walk the Dufferin Terrace boardwalk beneath the Chateau for the river view

name: Saint-Roch
why_fits: The revived lower-town district of the best restaurants, craft breweries and tech offices
why_caution: Down the hill from the walled town
local_tip: Saint-Roch is where locals eat and drink away from the old-town tourist prices

name: Montcalm
best_for: Couples seeking a calmer base|Culture lovers
why_fits: An elegant residential district by the Plains of Abraham park and the fine-arts museum
why_caution: Away from the old-town sights
local_tip: The Plains of Abraham battlefield park is a huge green space for a walk or picnic

name: Downtown
why_fits: The compact core between the harbor and False Creek, walkable to Stanley Park and the seawall
why_caution: Pricey, and busy with commuters
local_tip: Walk or bike the Stanley Park seawall, one of the world's great urban shoreline paths

name: Gastown
why_fits: The historic cobbled district of the steam clock, now full of restaurants and bars
why_caution: Borders the rougher Downtown Eastside -- be aware a block or two east
local_tip: Time a photo of the Gastown steam clock as it whistles on the quarter hour

name: Kitsilano
why_fits: A relaxed beachside district of Kits Beach, the pool and mountain-and-sea views across the bay
why_caution: A bridge from downtown, more residential
local_tip: Kitsilano Beach's saltwater pool and mountain backdrop are a summer favorite

name: Downtown
why_fits: The core around the CN Tower, waterfront and financial district, hyper-central and well linked
why_caution: Dense and pricey
local_tip: The PATH underground network links downtown blocks, handy in extreme weather

name: Kensington Market
why_fits: The bohemian, multicultural warren of vintage shops, cheap global eats and street murals
why_caution: Gritty-edged and busy
local_tip: Kensington Market beside Chinatown is the city's best-value area to eat and browse

name: Distillery District
why_fits: A pedestrian-only Victorian industrial district of galleries, boutiques and restaurants
why_caution: Small and can be quiet on weekdays
local_tip: The car-free cobbled lanes are especially lovely during the winter light market

name: Downtown
why_fits: The core around Pike Place Market and the waterfront, walkable to the main sights
why_caution: Steep hills and pricey parking
local_tip: Watch the fishmongers throw fish at Pike Place, then explore the market's lower levels

name: Capitol Hill
why_fits: The city's densest nightlife-and-dining district, creative, walkable and lively
why_caution: Loud on weekend nights
local_tip: Cal Anderson Park anchors this walkable, bar-and-cafe-lined neighborhood

name: Ballard
why_fits: A former Nordic fishing district, now a relaxed area of breweries, a Sunday market and the locks
why_caution: A drive or bus north of downtown
local_tip: Watch salmon and boats pass through the Ballard Locks in summer

name: French Quarter
why_fits: The historic heart of wrought-iron balconies, jazz clubs and Bourbon Street, walkable and alive
why_caution: Bourbon Street is loud, rowdy and seedy at night
local_tip: Skip Bourbon Street for the live jazz clubs on Frenchmen Street a few blocks over

name: Garden District
why_fits: A gracious district of antebellum mansions, oak-lined streets and the historic Lafayette Cemetery
why_caution: A streetcar ride from the Quarter, quiet at night
local_tip: Ride the historic St Charles streetcar through the mansion-lined avenue

name: Marigny
why_fits: The colorful Creole district next to the Quarter, home to the live-music bars of Frenchmen Street
why_caution: Edgier a few blocks from the main strip
local_tip: Frenchmen Street is where locals go for real live jazz, not Bourbon Street

name: Centro
why_fits: The civic heart around the Plaza de Armas, cathedral and presidential palace, well connected by metro
why_caution: Busy and pickpocket-prone in crowds
local_tip: Ride the funicular up Cerro San Cristobal for a view over the whole city and Andes

name: Bellavista
why_fits: The bohemian district at the foot of San Cristobal hill, full of bars, murals and Neruda's house
why_caution: Rowdy and best-guarded at night
local_tip: Visit La Chascona, Pablo Neruda's quirky Santiago house, in this district

name: Providencia
best_for: Business travelers|Couples seeking a calmer base
why_fits: A leafy, safe, upscale district of parks, cafes and good metro links, a favorite base
why_caution: More corporate and residential than lively
local_tip: It's widely considered the most comfortable, walkable base for a first visit

name: Avenida Paulista
why_fits: The iconic central avenue of skyscrapers, the MASP art museum and Sunday street closures
why_caution: A busy commercial spine
local_tip: On Sundays Avenida Paulista closes to cars and fills with performers and strollers

name: Vila Madalena
why_fits: The artsy district of bars, galleries and the graffiti-filled Beco do Batman alley
why_caution: Loud and packed on weekend nights
local_tip: Walk the Beco do Batman alley, an ever-changing open-air street-art gallery

name: Jardins
why_fits: The most exclusive district of designer boutiques, fine dining and leafy calm streets
why_caution: The priciest area in the city
local_tip: Oscar Freire street is the city's premier luxury-shopping stroll

name: La Candelaria
why_fits: The colonial old town of cobbled lanes, museums, the Gold Museum and street art, walkable
why_caution: Rougher after dark -- stick to busy streets at night
local_tip: The Gold Museum and Botero Museum are both free or cheap and world-class

name: Chapinero
why_fits: A large, lively district of bars, restaurants and the Zona G gourmet strip
why_caution: Varies block to block -- some parts livelier and safer than others
local_tip: Zona G within Chapinero is the city's best concentration of good restaurants

name: Zona Rosa
why_fits: The upscale Zona T district of malls, smart bars and hotels, one of the safest-feeling bases
why_caution: Pricier and more polished than central Bogota
local_tip: The pedestrian Zona T is a compact, safe hub of dining and nightlife

name: Miraflores
why_fits: The safe, upscale clifftop district of parks, the Larcomar mall and Pacific sunset views
why_caution: Pricier and touristy
local_tip: Walk or paraglide along the Malecon clifftop parks above the ocean at sunset

name: Barranco
why_fits: The bohemian seaside district of art galleries, bars and the romantic Bridge of Sighs
why_caution: Livelier and noisier at night
local_tip: Cross the Puente de los Suspiros (Bridge of Sighs) at dusk, a local tradition

name: Centro Historico
why_fits: The UNESCO colonial center of the Plaza Mayor, cathedral and grand balconied mansions
why_caution: Busy by day and best left after dark
local_tip: The catacombs beneath the San Francisco monastery are an eerie highlight

name: Centro Historico
why_fits: One of the Americas' best-preserved colonial old towns, dense with gilded churches and plazas
why_caution: Hilly, high-altitude and quiet after dark
local_tip: Climb to the top of the Basilica del Voto Nacional for a vertiginous city view

name: La Mariscal
why_fits: The 'Gringolandia' district of hostels, bars and the Plaza Foch nightlife, central and cheap
why_caution: Rowdy at night and requires street-smarts
local_tip: It's the backpacker hub for cheap beds, tours and a night out

name: La Floresta
why_fits: A leafy, arty residential district of cafes, an indie cinema and weekend food markets
why_caution: Mostly residential, a walk from the sights
local_tip: La Floresta's Ochoymedio cinema and weekend market draw a local creative crowd

name: Centro Historico
why_fits: The monumental center of the cathedral, plazas and the Hospicio Cabanas murals, walkable
why_caution: Busy and worn in patches
local_tip: See the Orozco murals inside the Hospicio Cabanas, a UNESCO site

name: Chapultepec
why_fits: The trendy Avenida Chapultepec-Lafayette district of bars, cafes and design shops
why_caution: Loud along the main avenue at night
local_tip: The Avenida Chapultepec median fills with a Friday-night art and food market

name: Tlaquepaque
why_fits: A charming crafts-and-arts town within the metro area, of colorful lanes and mariachi plazas
why_caution: A ride from central Guadalajara
local_tip: Tlaquepaque's El Parian plaza is the classic spot for mariachi and a margarita

name: Habana Vieja
why_fits: The UNESCO old town of restored plazas, colonial mansions and Hemingway's bars, walkable
why_caution: Touristy and crumbling in parts
local_tip: Have a mojito where Hemingway did at La Bodeguita, then wander the four old plazas

name: Vedado
why_fits: The mid-century district of the Malecon seawall, grand hotels, jazz clubs and the university
why_caution: Faded grandeur and patchy upkeep
local_tip: Sit on the Malecon seawall at sunset with locals, the city's living room

name: Centro Habana
why_fits: The densely lived-in district between the old town and Vedado, raw and authentically Cuban
why_caution: Crumbling, crowded and short on polish
local_tip: Stay in a casa particular here for the most genuine, affordable local welcome

name: Plaza de Armas
why_fits: The Inca-and-colonial heart around the grand main square, walkable to every central sight
why_caution: High altitude -- take it easy the first day, and touristy
local_tip: Rest and hydrate your first day; the altitude here is no joke at 3,400m

name: San Blas
best_for: Couples seeking a calmer base|Culture lovers
why_fits: The bohemian artisan quarter of steep cobbled lanes, workshops and viewpoint cafes above the plaza
why_caution: A steep uphill climb from the center
local_tip: The San Blas viewpoint terraces give the best photo over Cusco's red roofs

name: San Pedro
why_fits: The lively market district of cheap hostels and the San Pedro food market near the station
why_caution: Busier and grittier around the market
local_tip: Eat a cheap set lunch (menu) at the San Pedro market's food stalls

name: Centro Historico
why_fits: The walled old city of balconied mansions, plazas and ramparts, impossibly photogenic
why_caution: Touristy and hot, with persistent street vendors
local_tip: Walk the old city walls at sunset with a drink from a rampart bar

name: Getsemani
why_fits: The formerly rough, now vibrant district of street art, hostels and the buzzing Plaza Trinidad
why_caution: Livelier and rawer than the walled city
local_tip: Plaza de la Trinidad fills nightly with locals, street food and music

name: Bocagrande
why_fits: The modern high-rise beach strip on the peninsula, with hotels facing the Caribbean
why_caution: A Miami-style strip rather than a charming one; grey-sand beach
local_tip: It's the easiest in-city beach base, a short taxi from the old town

name: Tulum Pueblo
why_fits: The inland town where locals live, with the best-value food and rooms away from the beach
why_caution: No beach within walking distance -- you'll cycle or taxi to the coast
local_tip: Rent a bike in the pueblo to reach both the ruins and the beach cheaply

name: Tulum Beach
why_fits: The boho-chic beach-road strip of eco-resorts, beach clubs and jungle-fringed white sand
why_caution: Very expensive, congested road and limited power at times
local_tip: Book beach-club day passes if you're not staying on the pricey beach strip

name: Aldea Zama
why_fits: A newer planned residential district of condos between the town and beach
why_caution: Still developing, with unpaved streets in parts
local_tip: It's a calmer middle-ground base, a short cycle from both town and sand

name: Ciudad Vieja
why_fits: The old-town peninsula of the port market, plazas and colonial architecture
why_caution: Quiet and best-guarded after dark
local_tip: Lunch on grilled meat at the Mercado del Puerto, the old town's iron market hall

name: Pocitos
why_fits: A pleasant residential beach district on the Rio de la Plata, with a rambla promenade
why_caution: A city beach on the river estuary
local_tip: Walk or run the Pocitos rambla, the seafront promenade locals love

name: Centro
why_fits: The central district around Plaza Independencia and the pedestrian 18 de Julio avenue
why_caution: A busy working center
local_tip: Stand in Plaza Independencia between the old and new city, by the Artigas mausoleum

name: CBD
why_fits: The grid-city core of laneway cafes, arcades and trams, walkable and endlessly explorable
why_caution: Busy and pricey
local_tip: Hunt down the CBD's hidden laneways for street art and tiny specialty coffee bars

name: Fitzroy
why_fits: The original hip inner-north district of Brunswick Street bars, vintage shops and live music
why_caution: Lively and noisy at night
local_tip: Brunswick and Gertrude streets are the heart of Melbourne's bar-and-band scene

name: St Kilda
why_fits: The bayside district of the beach, Luna Park funfair and the Acland Street cake shops
why_caution: A tram ride from the center
local_tip: Watch the little penguins come ashore at the St Kilda breakwater at dusk

name: CBD
why_fits: The riverbend city core of shopping, dining and ferry access, walkable and warm year-round
why_caution: A corporate center, quieter on weekends
local_tip: Ride the free CityHopper ferry along the river for a cheap city cruise

name: Fortitude Valley
why_fits: Brisbane's entertainment district ('the Valley') of live-music venues, bars and Chinatown
why_caution: Loud and rowdy late at night
local_tip: The Valley is the city's live-music heartland most weekend nights

name: South Bank
why_fits: The riverside parklands of a man-made beach lagoon, museums and the Wheel of Brisbane
why_caution: A polished tourist precinct rather than a neighborhood
local_tip: Streets Beach, a free man-made lagoon, is a hit with families year-round

name: CBD
why_fits: The riverside city core beside Elizabeth Quay and the vast Kings Park botanic gardens
why_caution: A quiet center after office hours
local_tip: Walk up into Kings Park for a sweeping view over the river and skyline

name: Northbridge
why_fits: The compact entertainment district of bars, the cultural centre and diverse cheap eats
why_caution: Rowdy on weekend nights
local_tip: The Perth Cultural Centre's museum and gallery here are free to enter

name: Fremantle
why_fits: The characterful port town of heritage streets, the weekend markets and the historic prison
why_caution: A half-hour train ride from central Perth
local_tip: Tour the Fremantle Prison, a World Heritage convict site, then hit the markets

name: CBD
why_fits: The harbor-side core around the Viaduct, Sky Tower and ferry terminal, central and walkable
why_caution: A busy commercial center, pricey
local_tip: Catch a ferry from the downtown terminal to Devonport or the islands

name: Ponsonby
why_fits: The stylish inner-city district of Ponsonby Road's restaurants, bars and boutiques
why_caution: A ride or long walk from the waterfront
local_tip: Ponsonby Central food hall is a great one-stop for the area's dining scene

name: Devonport
why_fits: A charming seaside village across the harbor, with beaches, cafes and volcano viewpoints
why_caution: Reached by ferry, away from the city bustle
local_tip: Ride the ferry over and climb North Head's volcano for a harbor-and-city view

name: Te Aro
why_fits: The compact central district packed with cafes, the waterfront and Te Papa museum, all walkable
why_caution: Windy, and busy on weekends
local_tip: The huge Te Papa national museum on the waterfront is free and superb

name: Cuba Street
why_fits: The bohemian pedestrian strip of vintage shops, bars, cafes and the bucket fountain
why_caution: Lively and noisy at night
local_tip: Cuba Street is the city's counter-culture heart for coffee by day, bars by night

name: Oriental Bay
why_fits: Wellington's pretty in-city beach and promenade, a short stroll from the center
why_caution: A city beach, and breezy
local_tip: Walk the Oriental Bay promenade to the beach for a calm harbor swim in summer

name: Town Centre
why_fits: The compact lakeside hub of bars, restaurants and adventure operators, walkable to the water
why_caution: Very touristy and pricey
local_tip: This is where you book the bungee, jet-boat and Milford Sound day trips

name: Fernhill
why_fits: A quieter hillside district of lodges with sweeping lake-and-mountain views, near the center
why_caution: Steep, and a short drive or walk from town
local_tip: Its elevated lodges have some of the best Remarkables mountain views

name: Frankton
why_fits: A practical, better-value district by the airport and lake, with supermarkets and family motels
why_caution: Away from the town-centre buzz
local_tip: It's the handiest, cheaper base near the airport with lake access and shops

name: Nadi Town
why_fits: The practical gateway town near the airport, with cheap rooms, markets and the Sri Siva temple
why_caution: Not a beach base -- it's a functional transit town
local_tip: Visit the colorful Sri Siva Subramaniya Hindu temple at the edge of town

name: Wailoaloa Beach
why_fits: The closest beach to the airport, a laid-back strip of budget-to-mid beachfront stays
why_caution: A grey-sand beach, not the postcard Fiji sand
local_tip: It's the easiest first or last night by the sea, minutes from the airport

name: Denarau Island
why_fits: A gated resort island of big-name hotels, a golf course and the marina for island-hopping
why_caution: A resort bubble, pricey and separate from local life
local_tip: Denarau's marina is the main departure point for day trips to the outer islands

name: Male City
why_fits: The dense island-capital of markets, mosques and the fish market, a quick ferry from the airport
why_caution: One of the world's most crowded islands -- no beaches and little green space
local_tip: See the coral-stone Old Friday Mosque, then browse the waterfront fish market at dusk

name: Hulhumale
why_fits: A modern reclaimed island beside the airport, with a real public swimming beach and wide streets
why_caution: A planned, still-growing island without the classic resort feel
local_tip: Its public beach is free and calm -- the easiest sea swim in the greater Male area

name: Villingili
why_fits: A relaxed, car-light residential island a short ferry from the capital, with a small local beach
why_caution: Quiet, with limited dining and a ferry needed for everything
local_tip: The short ferry from Male drops you into a far calmer, greener island pace
